summary.intent: Triage a second round of Codex review findings on the PyPI sealed-file-set PR (#233) by verifying each against the code, and fix those that belong in the PR.
summary.outcome: All four claims were confirmed in code. The malformed sealed-filename issue (#3) was fixed by moving filename helpers into the model and validating ownership at manifest validation; `just ci` passed (92.77% coverage) and the change was committed and pushed. The Python-only credentialed build, pnpm mismatch, and NAPI path guess were left for user decisions or separate PRs.

repo: PyPI filename helpers (pypi_dist_filename_parts, is_pypi_wheel, is_pypi_sdist, pypi_dist_belongs_to) now live in callisto-model next to normalize_pypi_project_name, and the graph crate and registry parser reuse them instead of duplicating is_wheel/is_sdist.

Manifest validation in callisto-model now rejects sealed Python files not belonging to the set's package/version via the new ArtifactManifestError::ForeignDistributionFile, so it runs at manifest write and again at `release execute` verify before any effect.

The Python-only credential exposure is not new to the stack: `callisto release` builds and pushes the tag in one credentialed job, and the template's `zizmor: ignore[artipacked]` comment says the push needs persisted credentials. The only fix is moving Python-only workspaces onto the sealed multi-job route, which costs local `callisto release` for them.

pnpm detection is inconsistent: npm.rs treats pnpm-lock.yaml or pnpm-workspace.yaml as pnpm, but detect_npm_package_manager in registry_argv.rs only checks the lockfile, so a workspace-file-only pnpm project is published with `npm publish --workspace`.
Spec text for manifest validation lives in docs/specs/release.json (a very long single line, around line 293), so new rejection rules need a spec update there.

code.finding: Publish package-manager selector recognizes only pnpm-lock.yaml, disagreeing with discovery in npm.rs.
Workspace detection accepts either pnpm-lock.yaml or pnpm-workspace.yaml as pnpm.
NAPI target drift check guesses root/<package-name>/package.json, so packages under packages/ or with scoped names skip the cross-check (warning only).
Manifest validation previously checked roster, safe names, and extensions but not filename ownership by package/version; ownership was only checked later in pypi_files.rs.
Ownership check happened at PyPI file-set construction, after other publishes in a mixed release could already have landed.

workflow: Verify each externally reported review finding against the code before changing anything, and classify each as introduced by this PR or pre-existing.

Large multi-file edits were done via a Python script with count==1 assertions on each replacement; the heredoc form was refused as too complex, so the script was written with the Write tool and run separately with `python3 -I`.
Avoid tests that accept multiple different errors; use exact assertions.
Run `just ci` locally and check coverage before pushing; pre-existing out-of-scope bugs get separate PRs.

friction: The heredoc command containing the edit script was refused as too complex, forcing a switch to the Write tool.
Codex noted the saved Entire history was unavailable, so it could not tell whether earlier findings had been noticed.
The single-line docs/specs/release.json made locating spec text awkward, requiring grep -o with context windows.
open_items: Decide whether to move Python-only generated releases to the sealed multi-job route (credential-free build), which would cost local `callisto release` for those workspaces.
Fix the pnpm discovery vs publish package-manager mismatch in a separate PR (prioritized first).
Fix the NAPI drift check path guess in a separate PR.
Decide whether a hashless index should be an error for files this run uploads (currently accepted to avoid breaking private indexes).
Run one hosted release (build, partial upload, rerun) after #233 is merged, as Codex requested.
The newest push's CI run on #233 had not finished at the time of the summary.
